## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
The new `finished_at` column must be fixed before merge: it returns the start time of processes that are still running, because the source events contain no finish event. The documented meaning of NULL also disagrees with the query for processes that started and were later cleared.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `finished_at` column to the `processes` current-state model, computed from the latest event per process, and documents it in `models/schema.yml`. It also adds a one-line root-level `review.txt` that is unrelated to the model.

## Critical
- models/processes.sql:10 — correctness — `finished_at` returns the start time of running processes — Process 20, whose latest event is `started` at `2026-01-01T00:01:00Z`, gets that start time as `finished_at` although it has not finished. `sources/process_events.sql:4` allows only `created`, `started` and `cleared`, so no event marks a finish. — Consumers of `processes` read every still-running process as finished at its start time. — Fix: Either rename the column and its description to `started_at`, or take the timestamp from the event that marks completion; the event vocabulary does not settle which is intended.

## Important
- models/schema.yml:17 — comments — NULL documented as never started, also returned after clear — Process 30, started at event 3 and then `cleared` at event 4, gets NULL, which the description `NULL means the process has never been started.` labels as never started. `case when event_type = 'started' then occurred_at end` yields NULL whenever the latest event is not `started`. — Consumers who filter on NULL to find never-started processes also get processes that started and were later cleared. — Fix: If the timestamp should survive later events, compute it over all of the process's events instead of the `recency = 1` row; otherwise reword the line to say NULL means the latest event is not `started`.
